messages.subject: NULL model Best model, why?
parts:
Hello again everyone!

I have recently used the unmarked package to find the abundance of Ortalis vetula for a small scale study in Guatemala. There is something that is bugging me: in my analisis in unmarked, the NULL model is the best model according to the AIC. However, I had a bunch of Sitecovs and two obscov. So, the question is: does that mean my covariates doesn't have any impact on the abundance or does it mean I lack data?  The answer to this question will greatly impact my analysis and the following recommendation in my work. I linked the code I used and the data I used to this message.

Thanks!

Gabrielle

messages.author: 4a15de51da4445ae
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] NULL model Best model, why?
parts:
Dear Gabrielle,

 I believe the data set is sufficiently small that it is challenging to properly estimate all of the model parameters, especially with the NB model, and with such low detection probabilities. This issue is addressed in some detail by these two papers here which you'll have to read through and try to understand.
http://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/biom.12246/full
http://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/biom.12521/full
As a consequence I think you should probably rule out the NB model for this data set and default to the ZIP and Poisson models.
(also see the Kery and Royle book , Applied Hierarchical Modeling, chapter 6).
 Marc Kery has a relevant paper in review which I wonder if he'll provide on this email list?

 In reply to your specific question about whether this indicates a lack of effect of the covariate or a lack of power due to small sample size, this is not a question that can be answered definitively. You can do a power analysis to give you some ideas about power and sample size requirements which I highly recommend!

 Power to detect abundance effects is definitely affected strongly by the number of sites but also very important is the repeatability of counts: low detection (low repeatability of counts) leads to very low power to detect effects I think.

regards,
andy

messages.subject: Re: NULL model Best model, why?
parts:
Hello again,

I would first like to thank you for your quick answer, it helped me a lot to orientate the analysis of my study. I think I might do a power analysis too. I just want to be sure about something ,since I have never done a power analysis before for an N-mixture model. Do I simply have to run a simulation in R like in chapter 6 p. 246 of Applied Hierarchical
Modeling in Ecology vol.1?

Heres the code in question: 

# Define simulation settings and arrays for sim results
simreps <- 1000 # Simulate and analyse 1000 data sets
nsites <- c(20, 120, 250) # Levels for nsites factor
nreps <- c(2, 5, 10) # Levels of nrep factor
estimates <- array(NA, dim = c(2, simreps, 3, 3))

# Fill p with random numbers between 0.01 and 0.99
p <- array(runif(n=simreps*3*3, 0.01, 0.99), dim = c(simreps, 3, 3))
# Launch simulation (takes about 6.3 hours)

for(s in 1:3){ # Loop over levels of nsites factor
for(r in 1:3){ # Loop over levels of nreps factor
for(i in 1:simreps){ # Simulate and analyse 1000 data sets
cat("*** Simrep number", i, "***\n")
data <- simNmix(nsite=nsites[s], nvisit=nreps[r], mean.lam = 5,
mean.p=p[i,s,r], show.plot = F) # Generate data set
umf <- unmarkedFramePCount(y = data$C) # Bundle data for unmarked
fm <- pcount(~1 ~1, umf) # Fit model
estimates[,i,s,r] <- coef(fm) # Save estimates
}
}
}
# Visualization
par(mfrow = c(3,3), mar = c(4.5,4.5,2,2), cex.lab = 1.5, cex.axis = 1.3)
for(s in 1:3){ # Loop over nsites
for(r in 1:3){ # Loop over nreps
plot(p[,s,r], exp(estimates[1,,s,r]), xlab = "Detection probability",
ylab = "lambda_hat", main = "", ylim = c(0, 75), frame = F)
text(0.75, 60, paste("M = ", nsites[s], ", J = ", nreps[r], sep = ""),
cex = 1.5)
abline(h = 5, col = "red", lwd = 2)
lines(smooth.spline(exp(estimates[1,,s,r])~p[,s,r]), col="blue", lwd=2)
}
}

I saw there is an exercise of power analysis in chapter 4 but I wasn't able to find the exercise book for AHM. 

Thanks

Gabrielle
